newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly panel rejects call for tax review.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly panel rejects call for tax review.

text.p: A California Assembly committee on Monday rejected state Assemblyman Jan Goldsmith's request for an investigation of allegedly "unlawful" tax increases.

Goldsmith, a Republican, alleged last week that at least $34 billion in state tax increases -- imposed since the passage in 1978 of California's Proposition 13 -- were illegal because they were approved without a two-thirds vote of the legislature.
Goldsmith asked the Assembly Rules Committee on Monday to freeze the taxes and to authorize an investigation of these "unlawful tax hikes," according to a spokesman.
"The assemblyman asked the leadership to enforce the two-thirds vote requirement," spokesman Andrew Andersen said.
But the Assembly Rules Committee rejected the request on a party-line vote of 6-to-4, state officials said.
Goldsmith maintains that a two-thirds vote of the legislature is required on all state tax bills.
